The late afternoon sun cast long shadows across the lawn as Lena walked next door, a box of heavy-duty trash bags slung over her shoulder. "Ready to tackle the beast?" she called out, her voice cheerful. 

Mr. Harding, her neighbor of three years, stood on his porch, a slightly harried expression on his face. He was a man of quiet habits, a retired history professor who seemed to prefer the company of his books to that of people. Yet, he'd been surprisingly welcoming since they'd moved in, always offering a wave and a pleasant, if brief, greeting. “Lena, so glad you could make it. It’s gotten…unwieldy, to say the least,” he said, gesturing towards the small, detached storage room tucked behind his garage. "I’ve been putting it off, of course, but it’s become an obstacle to the lawnmower."

The storage room was, as he’d described, an absolute mess. Boxes were stacked haphazardly, draped with cobwebs and coated in a layer of dust. Old furniture, gardening tools, and miscellaneous knick-knacks competed for space, creating a chaotic jumble. Lena set down the bags and surveyed the scene. “Okay, operation declutter begins now. Let's grab some gloves and start sorting. We’ll need a system. How about we create piles: keep, donate, trash?”

Mr. Harding nodded, his worry lines softening slightly. “That sounds sensible. I've got some work gloves in the garage, and a few old tarps we can use to cover things we don’t want to get dusty immediately.” He disappeared into the garage, returning a moment later with the promised items. "I was hoping to finish this up today, but my daughter called. She’s coming over for dinner unexpectedly, and I need to start prepping. Perhaps we should take a break around six?”

“Absolutely,” Lena agreed. “A good hour will give us time to regroup and maybe grab some iced tea. I’ll bring some cookies from the bakery – their chocolate chip are heavenly.” Mr. Harding’s face lit up a fraction. “That’s very kind of you, Lena. My daughter adores those cookies.”

An hour later, the aroma of freshly baked cookies and the clinking of ice in glasses filled the air as they sat on the porch, taking a breather. The storage room, while still a significant challenge, looked marginally more organized. A ‘donate’ pile was growing steadily, and a small, disheartening heap of trash was accumulating. Mr. Harding seemed to have visibly relaxed, his shoulders less tense. "Thank you again for your help, Lena. I truly appreciate it."



Lena smiled, wiping a stray crumb from her chin. “It’s really no trouble. A little organization can do wonders. Now, let’s get back to it. I think we’ve only scratched the surface.” She stood, retrieved a pair of gloves, and headed back towards the storage room, ready to face the remaining chaos.
